author: Codex /root/libertarian_historical (research author; AI-assisted)
changeNote: Replaces the mismatched higher-phase ideal with the explicitly narrowed Chinese Marxist–Leninist governing tradition for 2022–2026. All 240 exact propositions reassessed anew; no old score or answer carried forward. Formal rules, actual governance and current acts are distinguished. Unknowns are retained where comparative or policy-specific evidence is missing.

metadata.name: Communism
metadata.description: The CPC’s contemporary socialism with Chinese characteristics: Party-led government, strategic public ownership, regulated markets and national sovereignty.
metadata.scope: The contemporary CPC governing tradition and its socialism with Chinese characteristics, assessed through its 2022 programme and mainland Chinese laws and policy acts in force or adopted during 2022–2026. Earlier legal foundations are used where still operative. This is one expressly narrowed communist tradition, not every communist school, all Chinese citizens, or the Marx–Engels higher-phase ideal. Formal institutions are checked against governing practice; Taiwan policy is reported as the PRC’s position without endorsing its territorial claims. Unresolved questions remain unknown, not neutral. No complete placement can be published while these remain.
metadata.phrase: A Party-led socialist state combining strategic public ownership and regulated markets with national sovereignty and coordinated development.

axes.brief: Party monopoly excludes competitive leadership and independent opposition. Formal suffrage and congress removal powers must not be mistaken for competitive national democracy.
axes.counterEvidence: The constitution includes elections, recall and supervision, but independent monitoring documents Party control. Some precise institutional alternatives remain unresolved.

answers.rationale: National leadership is selected within Party-controlled institutions, without competitive public elections.
Party selection is not identical to selection by an independent expert panel; the precise alternative is unestablished.
Article 34 excludes education-based voting restrictions, although political-rights deprivation and Party vetting limit participation.
Articles 58 and 89 reserve statutes to the legislature; executive regulations remain legally subordinate.
Opposition parties cannot compete independently with the CPC; permitted parties must accept its leadership.
Independent organised opposition is excluded, including its proposed parliamentary scrutiny role.
Party supervision of courts excludes independent constitutional checks against the governing leadership.
Party-led congress selection excludes substitution of an autonomous trade-union selectorate.
Maintaining CPC leadership requires exclusion of organisations challenging its governing monopoly.
The checked framework supplies no popular legislative-repeal referendum procedure or explicit rejection of this particular mechanism.
Central Party organs determine major policy; collective organs qualify the proposition's claim of sole authority.
Article 63 provides legislative removal, while Party control prevents independent parliamentary enforcement: a documented institutional conflict.
Article 60 requires a two-thirds Standing Committee decision, rather than a leader's unilateral postponement.

Electoral Law articles 49–53 allow voters to petition for recall of county and township representatives, with a secret vote and majority of the original electorate required; qualified support reflects the local scope and Party-controlled institutions.
Party supremacy largely displaces electoral accountability, notwithstanding formal congress supervision.
The Party's absolute command of the armed forces expressly rejects autonomous military replacement of civilian leadership.

axes.brief: Speech, online identity and firearms evidence supports state authority in specific areas. Detailed search, detention and personal-health thresholds remain separate questions.
axes.counterEvidence: Formal rights protections and civil privacy rules coexist with repression; no general authoritarian label supplies every police power.

answers.rationale: The checked sources do not provide the exact personal-drug-risk prescription; general authoritarianism is insufficient.
Article 40 permits investigative surveillance by public-security bodies; court-authorised serious-crime surveillance is a narrower permitted inference.
Permission requirements and suppression of peaceful protests contradict this broad protection for obstructive demonstrations.
Punishment of political criticism contradicts protection even for offensive institutional criticism.
The sources do not distinguish self-protective health compulsion from measures protecting other people.
Mass surveillance is documented, but the checked evidence does not establish the specified multi-year retention rule.
No checked traffic-enforcement provision establishes suspicionless intoxication testing.
Preventive detention is documented, but the question's court-found future-harm threshold requires a distinct provision.
State censorship of online and published material rejects unrestricted adult access to prohibited content.
Real-name verification and the 2025 digital identification initiative reject a general right to anonymous services.
The evidence does not establish this precise threat-based suspicionless-search power.
The permit-and-public-order approach permits prevention of disorderly gatherings; this is narrower than documented suppression.

Criminal procedure regulations articles 222–224 permit searches of homes with county-level police-chief approval and a police search warrant; prior court authorisation is not required even for ordinary non-emergency searches.
State-secret restrictions lack the proposed general misconduct-publication exception.
Gun Law articles 3–6 limit possession to specified official, sporting and hunting purposes; general defensive ownership is excluded.
Six-month residential surveillance is documented, but not detention lasting indefinitely until officials consider every threat resolved.

axes.brief: A shared Chinese identity is promoted alongside formal recognition of ethnic nationalities. Current assimilation practices constrain official cultural-plurality commitments.
axes.counterEvidence: Domestic ethnic-nationality policy is not automatically a migrant-integration policy. Funding, calendars and signage need their own evidence.

answers.rationale: The Party prioritises common Chinese identity and ideological cohesion when cultural commitments conflict.
Minority recognition does not establish extra spending to accommodate the particular public-service practices contemplated.
The checked national-identity programme does not specify migrants' obligation to adopt cultural customs.
Domestic ethnic protections are not automatically a rule for retaining foreign cultural identities after settlement.
The documented extension of Mandarin-medium education supports national-language priority; services beyond education require qualification.
Representation of recognised nationalities does not establish the proposed ceremonial recognition of Indigenous peoples.
The source does not specify predominant-tradition shares of cultural grants.
Common national unity takes precedence over separate identities under the Party programme.
A shared public calendar alone would not prove that accommodation is rejected.
Article 4 recognises multiple nationalities and their customs, although current assimilation policies constrain that recognition.
No checked migrant integration programme establishes this participation-versus-separation prescription.
Minority-language protections do not establish foreign-language signage duties for migrant communities.
The programme promotes a common Chinese national community over competing sectional identities.
The checked religious restrictions do not establish the exact face-covering exception posed here.
Formal protection of minority customs coexists with assimilationist governance: an evidenced conflict over cultural plurality.
The sources address nationalities and citizens more directly than migrant integration-programme content.

axes.brief: Residence and work rely on state permits and selected grounds. Refugee recognition, permanent settlement and ordinary labour admission are distinct.
axes.counterEvidence: No annual quota, cultural preference or universal sponsorship rule is inferred from selectivity alone; detailed permanent-residence regulations remain a research gap.

answers.rationale: Selectivity is documented, but not a national annual ceiling calculated from housing and labour deficits.
Residence requires state approval and specified grounds, rather than a general entitlement to improve living conditions.
The statute allows humanitarian grounds and other residence categories beyond economically important skills.
The checked entry law does not settle the scope of permanent residents' family-reunification entitlement.
The framework distinguishes recognised refugee residence from permanent residence, which requires separate approval.
The law requires departure when lawful stay expires and penalises unlawful residence; no general right to remain follows.
Articles 41–42 require permits and state-defined employment needs beyond an employer's wish to recruit.
No checked provision gives housing and service pressure priority over immigration's economic benefits.
Neither a shared family quota nor the relevant general annual ceiling is established.
A job offer alone does not replace the work-permit and residence-permit requirements.
The statute refers permanent-residence criteria to further rules; universal sponsorship is not established.
Graduation is not an automatic permanent status in the checked statute, but whether it alone supplies a route requires detailed admission regulations.
Article 46 provides refugee screening, but does not address admission after ordinary numerical limits are exhausted.
The checked criteria do not establish cultural similarity as an immigration preference.
Protection of foreigners' lawful interests does not specify cash-welfare or social-housing eligibility.
Economic opening does not establish a cultural-diversity rationale for increasing immigration.

axes.brief: The scoped tradition promotes national defence and peaceful diplomacy while retaining coercive options over Taiwan. This is not absolute pacifism.
axes.counterEvidence: Universal conscription, autonomous weapons and overseas campaigns require specific evidence; a military modernisation objective does not settle all these questions.

answers.rationale: The 2025 Taiwan statement retains force as an option beyond responding to an armed attack.
The same statement prioritises peaceful reunification while retaining military options.
World-class military modernisation does not establish willingness to bear the specified substantial financial cost specifically for superiority over opponents.
The checked statements do not establish the exact imminent-attack evidence threshold for pre-emption.
Retaining force for reunification rejects an exclusively attack-response doctrine.

Articles 3 and 19–21 combine a voluntary mainstay with selective compulsory male enlistment. This supports a male service duty, but does not settle the question if understood as general compulsory completion by male citizens.
The stated reunification commitment limits willingness to surrender core territorial aims solely to prevent conflict.
No checked weapon policy establishes autonomous target engagement without human approval.
The constitution assigns the armed forces defence and resistance to aggression, qualified by territorial force options.
The retained military option rejects avoiding force under every circumstance.
World-class-force aspirations alone do not establish an explicit prolonged overseas-combat prescription.
The 2025 policy retains force rather than committing to leave the Taiwan dispute indefinitely unresolved.
An expressly retained force option is used to deter separatist outcomes and external intervention.
Peaceful reunification is preferred, but military resolve is explicitly retained; neither priority is unconditional.
No checked doctrine establishes the exact espionage-versus-diplomatic-cost tradeoff.
Peaceful-development language does not specify accepting negotiated military-capability reductions.

axes.brief: Sovereignty and noninterference strongly constrain international authority, while negotiated cooperation and development projects are supported.
axes.counterEvidence: Treaty cooperation is distinct from supranational jurisdiction. Monetary pooling and particular judicial conflicts remain unresolved.

answers.rationale: The Party's sovereignty and noninterference principles favour final domestic authority.
Sovereignty-centred cooperation rejects unrestricted external decisions over national objections.
Sovereignty commitments do not specify the exact domestic-versus-international judicial conflict rule.
International cooperation is established; alliances constraining independent action need more specific evidence.
Constitution article 81 places treaty abrogation within domestic institutions, supporting domestic withdrawal authority.
The sources do not establish acceptance or rejection of every international court's jurisdiction over officials.
Safeguarding sovereignty and development interests qualifies external collective goals.
Environmental cooperation does not establish delegated international decision-making power.
An independent foreign policy and noninterference weigh against compulsory common bloc policies.
Noninterference and domestic political supremacy weigh against externally compelled legal changes.
Domestic monetary regulation does not establish whether monetary powers should be shared internationally. A specific sovereignty-of-currency position is still needed.
The programme supports joint international development through shared projects and cooperation, without general supranational rule.
Entry Law article 4 assigns entry administration to domestic state institutions.
The 2026 schedule implements negotiated tariff rates with 34 partners under 24 agreements, supporting acceptance of common trade commitments.
National sovereignty and the unitary constitutional state exclude transfer into an international political federation.
Shared-future rhetoric does not establish accepting enforcement costs when neutrality better serves immediate interests.

axes.brief: Public-sector leadership coexists with explicit support for private enterprise. The 2025 private-sector legislation prevents treating every business as state-owned.
axes.counterEvidence: Counting most enterprises differs from strategic control. Sector-specific utilities, banks, infrastructure and provider-contract choices require more direct evidence.

answers.rationale: The 2025 private-sector law supports a sector comprising most enterprises; public strategic leadership remains a qualification.
General public-sector leadership does not establish ownership of every essential utility network.
The 2025 law requires fair competition across ownership forms while the Party retains public-sector leadership.
The constitutional commitment to grow the state sector rejects leaving competitive production entirely private.
Healthcare access commitments do not determine public-versus-private facility ownership.

The state transferred national railway assets into a wholly state-owned corporation responsible for passenger transport and network construction; the 2019 successor retained state ownership. This supports public infrastructure without claiming every individual railway has exclusive public ownership.
Purchasing social assistance services is endorsed, but the cited policy does not establish preferring private providers specifically on comparable-quality/lower-cost grounds.
The PBC 2025 stability report records six large state-owned commercial banks alongside nineteen private banks, and supports continued development of this differentiated banking system.
Consolidation of the public sector rejects a general programme of selling state commercial businesses.
Housing aid and public-rental provision do not establish the substantial publicly owned rental-stock share requested.
State-sector leadership in strategically important activity opposes relying exclusively on private ownership and regulation.
State ownership of mineral resources is distinct from ownership of extraction businesses.
Purchasing social assistance services does not establish a general waste-collection contracting preference.
The commitment to consolidate the public sector supports retaining strategic ownership rather than revenue-led divestment.
The sources do not determine sale versus retention of a repeatedly subsidised state business.
State media ownership and Party direction support retaining national public broadcasting.

axes.brief: Foreign investment has national treatment outside an explicit restrictive list. Retaliatory tariffs coexist with negotiated suspensions and opening measures.
axes.counterEvidence: Investment, imports, procurement and product taxation are different instruments. Evidence for one is not automatically a position on another.

answers.rationale: Retaliatory tariffs are established; that does not alone establish general protection from ordinary foreign competition.
Opening foreign investment is distinct from removing most trade barriers despite domestic losses.
No checked procurement rule establishes the specified domestic-price preference.
The checked investment rules do not determine freedom to source all goods across countries.
Strategic investment restrictions do not establish import restrictions on essential goods.
The 2026 schedule unilaterally lowers duties on selected goods and maintains zero tariffs for least-developed partners; support is selective, not universal.
The checked policy does not establish temporary infant-industry import restrictions with consumer-price costs.
National treatment outside the negative list coexists with sector-specific foreign ownership restrictions.
Foreign restrictions on seed production and fishing concern investment, not agricultural import protection.
The sources do not settle adjustment versus trade protection across domestic businesses.
The 2025 tariff measures expressly retaliated against United States export tariffs.
No checked tax provision establishes equal product taxes across domestic and foreign products.
No checked countervailing-duty provision establishes this subsidy-based import restriction.
Treaty preferences are recognised, but removal of tariffs despite import dependence is not established.
The negative list bars or caps foreign control in nuclear power, rare-earth extraction and other strategic sectors.
Foreign investment restrictions govern ownership of providers; they do not alone establish special restrictions on consumers buying foreign online services.

axes.brief: Market pricing and enterprise decisions coexist with macroeconomic steering, minimum wages and monetary restrictions.
axes.counterEvidence: National plans do not automatically imply compulsory output targets. Directed credit, subsidies, outbound capital and rents remain separately assessed.

answers.rationale: The private-sector law protects enterprise development and fair competition within the socialist market framework.
National planning does not necessarily impose compulsory firm-level output quantities.
Pricing Law articles 3 and 6 make market prices the default, with limited guided or fixed exceptions.
The Party programme endorses structural steering and coordinated national development rather than wholly autonomous investment allocation.
Support for private enterprise and market allocation favours demand-led business decisions, qualified by industrial steering.
Pricing Law article 18 authorises controls for specified essential and monopoly goods and services.
The 2025 law promotes fair market access rather than a universal test that additional output is needed.
Macroeconomic steering does not itself establish directed bank credit for the exact selected industries.
The checked sources do not establish the detailed outbound capital approval regime.
Sectoral development goals do not identify the specified subsidy-versus-private-investor tradeoff.
The 2026 joint notice prohibits private virtual-currency monetary circulation and related unapproved financial activity.
Labour Law article 48 expressly establishes minimum wages, implemented through regional standards.
Articles 33 and 47 permit collective agreements and enterprise wage determination; minimum standards remain binding.
The sources do not establish the central bank's exact subordination for lending and rate decisions.
General market pricing does not settle rental-specific controls and exceptions.
The programme expressly combines decisive markets with macroeconomic coordination: neither comprehensive planning nor wholly uncoordinated enterprise choice.

axes.brief: Progressive income taxation and targeted assistance are established. Assistance includes differentiated basic and near-threshold hardship support.
axes.counterEvidence: Public services and public ownership do not prove cash-income equalisation. Wealth and inheritance taxes and several benefit tradeoffs remain unresolved.

answers.rationale: Progressive income taxation and targeted assistance support redistribution, without claiming Nordic-scale equalisation.

Congress report IX(1) expressly uses taxation to regulate excessive incomes for common prosperity and prevent polarisation, making income distribution an independent policy objective, while protecting lawful earnings.
The checked assistance expansion does not establish acceptance of higher taxes for a stronger minimum income.
The 2023 policy centres basic-living and targeted hardship protection rather than comprehensive income equalisation.
Article 3 sets rising marginal rates on comprehensive income, from 3 to 45 percent.
The sources do not determine this explicit retention-versus-household-inequality tradeoff.
No checked rule prescribes inheritance taxation to finance income transfers.
Dynamic eligibility reviews are not a fixed time limit while low income continues.
Taxing income from property is not a tax on accumulated wealth funding transfers.
Targeted assistance alone does not establish modest benefits specifically to lower taxpayers' burden.
Social-inclusion services are not evidence that cash benefits cover ordinary participation beyond survival.
The checked policy does not rank tax reductions against increased cash benefits.
The assistance framework recognises working low-income households and employment-cost deductions; income supplementation is conditional, not universal.
Progressive marginal income-tax bands expressly reject equal marginal rates across high and ordinary earnings.
Collective land tenure is not compensated redistribution of private large landholdings under this proposal.
Basic cash aid targets severe need, while additional aid includes near-threshold and high-essential-expense households; the scope is deliberately differentiated.

axes.brief: Party-state and civil institutions govern law and religion; official schooling excludes cultivation of religious faith.
axes.counterEvidence: Restriction of religion does not establish every ceremony, holiday, symbol or tax rule. Secularity is not equivalent to religious liberty.

answers.rationale: Civil law rests on constitutional and socialist authority rather than religious doctrine.
The legal framework does not assign religious teaching legislative authority.
Party-led state institutions govern religious affairs rather than requiring clergy's approval.
The constitution defines a socialist state, not one founded on a particular religion.
The official education policy rejects proselytising, but also restricts religion courses; neutral comparative teaching is not clearly prescribed.
The official school policy excludes instruction cultivating religious faith.
State civil-law institutions govern family relations; religious rulings are not the source of the Civil Code.
State control over religious bodies does not establish whether they have an official advisory role in reviewing proposed laws; the question does not require independent review.
Atheist Party identity does not alone establish the content of every state ceremony.
Religious-site administration is not evidence of funding activities intended to strengthen belief.
No checked buildings policy specifies this particular religious-symbol rule.
The sources do not establish holidays retained as official recognition of a predominant religion.
Legislative selection rests on state electoral units; religious office does not itself confer a constitutional seat.
No checked tax rule establishes a religion-specific exemption beyond charitable treatment.
Civil Code articles 1046–1049 make marriage a voluntary civil registration matter, without religious approval.
The Civil Code places family-law validity under civil institutions, supporting rejection of binding religious-court alternatives.

axes.brief: The programme combines selective traditional culture with reform; civil marriage law remains opposite-sex and promotes marital family virtues.
axes.counterEvidence: Legal equality is not the same as universal social acceptance. Specific abortion, dress, sexuality-education and gender-language positions remain unestablished.

answers.rationale: The Party combines reform and innovation with deliberate preservation and transformation of selected traditional culture.
Selected inherited culture is promoted, while feudal practices are rejected and traditions may be transformed.
Civil rights for children outside marriage do not alone establish identical social recognition for every household form.
Equal legal status and family duties do not establish society's preferred gender-role differentiation.
Civil Code article 1046 defines entry into marriage through a man and a woman.
Civil Code marital fidelity and family virtues do not establish a societal preference for the specific two-parent married household over other family forms.
No checked source establishes social acceptance of elective early abortion; legality and prevalence would not suffice.
State curriculum control does not settle this exact parental objection to sexual-values instruction.
The checked adoption principles do not establish social acceptance of same-sex adoptive couples.
No checked doctrine establishes a general traditional modest-dress expectation for public life.
The materials do not prescribe adapting language conventions to personal gender identification.
Promoting selected inherited virtues alongside cultural innovation does not establish priority for passing existing moral customs over new ones.
Oppression of LGBT organising does not establish every cross-sex traditional-role acceptance comparison.
Pragmatic reform rhetoric does not settle gradualism even when faster institutional change is popular.
The checked education and censorship sources do not specify descriptive teaching about sexual orientation and gender identity.
Rejecting feudal practices does not settle preserving otherwise harmless inherited customs whose practical purpose is unclear.

axes.brief: The BCI guidelines directly support cautious, supervised enhancement research. Ecological protection qualifies technological and infrastructure development.
axes.counterEvidence: No blanket technological optimism is inferred. Embryo laboratory research differs from reproductive trials; medical AI and GM thresholds require further evidence.

answers.rationale: Innovation promotion does not define a general early-benefit threshold for widespread deployment despite unknown long-term harm.
Technology-specific ethics rules do not establish a universal small-trial-only rule for every technology.
The ecological programme does not identify when substantial infrastructure benefits justify permanent habitat loss.
BCI-specific safety research requirements do not establish a general long-term-study rule for all medical technologies.
Retraining policy acknowledges AI transition but does not explicitly accept replacing many jobs as the condition of adoption.
The Party expressly prioritises environmental protection, qualified by its simultaneous development commitment.
No checked food-technology policy establishes cultivated-meat replacement before long-term environmental evidence.

The guidelines require sufficient evidence for invasive research and moderation for enhancement, but do not expressly define the proposed research-only restriction until strong long-term safety evidence. Section 5.4 specifically concerns non-invasive enhancement.
The programme expressly prioritises resource conservation, opposing displacement of consumption reduction by unproven technological fixes.
A conservation priority does not establish the exact project-delay threshold while environmental effects remain unknown.

General sections 3.2 and 4.1 require properly managed risks and sufficient safety-and-benefit evidence even for invasive research, supporting qualified rejection of access on basic safety alone. This normative inference does not treat the non-invasive enhancement section 5.4 as an implant-specific rule.
The checked BCI safeguards do not establish diagnostic-AI reliability thresholds across patient groups.
The 2024 guideline prohibits reproductive germline trials but not all laboratory embryo research; the question does not distinguish them.
No checked GM-crop rule establishes the exact long-term ecosystem-evidence threshold.
Environmental protection is prioritised while urbanisation and development are promoted; land-use choices are conditionally balanced.
The checked technology-specific guidelines do not establish a universal irreversibility-based delay rule.

axes.brief: Local initiative and ethnic autonomy operate under central constitutional leadership. The national state retains territorial and emergency powers.
axes.counterEvidence: Some provincial fiscal discretion and local implementation survive; this is not proof of constitutionally sovereign regional power.

answers.rationale: Constitution article 3 places local initiative under unified central leadership.
Article 89 assigns central supervision and annulment of inappropriate local decisions.
Article 4 prohibits secession and makes autonomous areas inseparable parts of the state.
Article 89 permits annulment of local-government decisions despite local support.
Regional autonomy operates within national law, not independent regional constituent authority.
National public-security administration coexists with local agencies; the precise single-command preference is unestablished.
No checked fiscal allocation rule settles retaining most locally collected tax revenue.
National ideological curriculum requirements constrain regional choice over compulsory study.

Resource Tax Law article 2 permits provincial governments and legislatures to select applicable tax rates within national bands; qualified support recognises actual regional rate variation under central limits.
National Labour Law fixes working-time and employment protections, while permitting limited regional implementation.
Constitution article 89 assigns territorial divisions to central approval rather than unilateral local voters.
National health administration does not establish uniform coverage decisions for every medical treatment.
Article 4 promises ethnic territorial self-government but subordinates it to a unitary, centrally led state.
Nationally prescribed income-tax bands and bounded local relief reject unrestricted tax competition.
Resource ownership and national ecological goals do not settle purely intraregional land-and-wildlife discretion.
The centre's constitutional emergency and unified-administration powers support national direction across affected regions.

axes.brief: The checked contemporary sources prescribe education, equality and development, but do not settle the sixteen comparative empirical-causation claims.
axes.counterEvidence: No higher-phase Marxist anthropology, government-funded scientific paper or presumed collectivist psychology is substituted for a declared governing-tradition position.

answers.rationale: Political education seeks behavioural change, but does not establish the comparative weight of upbringing and inherited tendencies.
No checked Party doctrine or government text establishes a hereditary explanation of cross-country IQ differences.
Legal gender equality does not establish whether socialisation or biology explains more observed behavioural differences.
No checked source ranks biological and experiential causes of stress sensitivity.
Skills development policy does not establish the relative inherited and experiential causes of personal interests.
Pragmatic risk management is not a theory of inherited individual risk-taking tendencies.
Promoting collective values does not establish a comparative causal claim about cooperative habits and heredity.
No checked source ranks inherited capacities versus upbringing as causes of empathy differences.
Attention-enhancement research does not establish whether existing attention differences arise more from experience than inheritance.
Moral education policy does not establish that immediate moral reactions are mainly learned rather than biologically predisposed.
Security narratives and public education do not rank the causes of individual threat perception.
No checked contemporary doctrinal or government text supplies the temperament comparison.
No checked source establishes the relative influence of culture and inheritance on physical-attractiveness preferences.
Ethnic equality and anti-discrimination commitments do not establish the question's racial-violence causal comparison.
Party discipline and re-education do not by themselves establish the comparative contribution of inherited racial tendencies to self-control.
Equal-pay rules express a legal standard, not an explanation of the aggregate gender pay gap.

review.notes: Separate literal-wording review of all 240 questions under the newly specified Chinese Marxist-Leninist governing tradition, 2022-2026. Primary CPC/PRC texts were checked against Freedom House institutional research, with explicit distinction between formal legal provisions and governing practice. State absence was not treated as competitive democracy. Removed unsupported official religious-review, preferred two-parent family, and implant-specific long-term research-only inferences. Fresh targeted research supports local recall, police rather than court search warrants, national rail ownership, and mixed public/private banking. All numeric answers were reviewed individually; all 128 unanswered records remain unresolved, not Neutral. This is a completed evidence-review pass on an incomplete research draft, not approval to publish. No target scores were consulted. Detailed decisions and access limits are recorded in peer-communism.json and the research dossier.
